facts.fact: The Births and Deaths Registration Act (Chapter 5:02, consolidated to 6 March 2020) requires each district registrar to keep registers in the prescribed form and to sign and forward all notices of births, still-births and deaths, with medical certificates, to the Registrar-General by registered post; the Act makes no provision for an electronic register or record. This is the statute's prescription, not a report of practice.

The Act places the registers under a Registrar-General of Births and Deaths, a public-service office that is the central registering office, with a registrar for each district, and assigns the Act's administration to the Minister of Home Affairs (text as consolidated to 6 March 2020).

systems.owner: Registrar-General of Births and Deaths, under the Minister of Home Affairs
systems.tiers: a registrar for each district, and the Registrar-General's office as central registering office

note: A statute: it names no information system and no software. Both facts are what the law prescribes, dated to the consolidation of 6 March 2020; the Act itself commenced on 20 June 1986.
